rationale.color_psychology: Deep lichen green carries continuity, patience, and living systems without the bright eco-tech shorthand. Cambium copper names the growth layer and introduces human warmth. Bone and bark neutrals make the system feel archival and tactile rather than synthetic.
rationale.competitor_differentiation: The category leans on electric blue, violet gradients, neon accents, and black-glass dashboards. Cambium uses botanical darks, mineral warmth, and paper-like neutrals, so the identity reads as stewardship and instrumentation rather than AI spectacle.

primary.name: Living Lichen
primary.usage: Primary brand field, headlines, navigation, key line work, and the stable outer boundary in diagrams.

secondary.name: Cambium Copper
secondary.usage: Human decisions, founder gates, active growth rings, selected states, and small emphasis fields; pair with Ink, never white body text.

accent.name: New Growth
accent.usage: Positive viability margin, safe inward trajectories, new evidence, and quiet highlights paired with Ink text.

restricted_pairs: Do not use white text on Cambium Copper; measured contrast is 3.95:1.
Do not use white text on New Growth; measured contrast is 3.11:1.

do: Use as the dominant field or the darkest structural line.
Pair with Bone for long-form reading.
Let large dark areas breathe with generous margins.
dont: Do not turn it into a generic sustainability claim.
Do not combine with neon green.
Do not use every green variation in one surface.

do: Reserve for human choice and living growth.
Use Ink for text on copper fields.
Keep copper under roughly fifteen percent of a composition.
dont: Do not use as an error state.
Do not set small white type on it.
Do not render it as glossy metallic chrome.
